seoTitle: How to Archive Workspace Email Instead of Deleting a User
metaDescription: Learn how to archive a Google Workspace user's email instead of deleting the account, preserving data for compliance while saving on billing.
intro: When an employee leaves, deleting their account outright can mean losing important emails you're legally or operationally required to keep. This guide covers how to archive their Workspace email instead, preserving the data while cutting billing costs.

steps.heading: Suspend the departing user's account
steps.body: Rather than deleting immediately, suspend the account first to pause active access while keeping the data intact.

steps.heading: Assign a data retention policy
steps.body: Set retention rules so the user's emails and files are preserved for the length of time your organization requires for compliance.

steps.heading: Use Google Vault or export options
steps.body: If your plan includes Google Vault, use it to retain and search archived data; otherwise, export the data to another archive-friendly format.

steps.heading: Convert to an archived user license
steps.body: Switch the account to an archived-user status to reduce its licensing cost while keeping the mailbox accessible to admins.

steps.heading: Transfer ownership of Drive files
steps.body: Reassign ownership of important Drive files to another active user so shared documents remain accessible after the account is archived.

faq.question: How long does archived data stay accessible in Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Archived data generally remains accessible for as long as the account stays in archived status, subject to your organization's retention policy.

faq.question: Is archiving cheaper than keeping a full user license active?
faq.answer: Yes, an archived-user license typically costs less than a standard active license while still preserving the data.

faq.question: Do I need Google Vault to archive a user's email?
faq.answer: Google Vault makes retention and legal hold easier, but you can also archive a user and preserve data without it depending on your plan.

faq.question: What happens to Drive files owned by an archived user?
faq.answer: It's best to transfer ownership of important shared files to an active user before archiving, so collaborators don't lose access.
